newsitem.title: UK: British Gas looses 2000 domestic users a week-Ofgas.
newsitem.headline: British Gas looses 2000 domestic users a week-Ofgas.

text.p: Residential gas consumers in the south west of England are now changing from British Gas to other suppliers at the rate of 2,000 a week, an Ofgas spokesman said on Monday.

Chris Webb, Director of Public Affairs at regulator Ofgas told an industry conference that over 80,000 customers out of a total of a little over 500,000 in the first "pilot area" had switched by the end of November.
He added that the total was expected by at least one alternative supplier to reach 100,000, or nearly 20 percent of the market, by the end of this year.
Deregulation in the domestic market, allowing residential consumers to buy gas from any licensed supplier, began in a pilot area of Devon, Cornwall and Somerset on 29 April.
A second pilot area containing around another 1.5 million consumers in Avon, Dorset, Kent, East and West Sussex will open for competition in two phases on 10 February and 7 March.
The whole of Britain will be opened to competition during 1998. Webb said that nationwide introduction of competition is likely to be staggered.
"We have not made up our minds on the timetable yet, but you can take it as read it will be introduced in stages", he said.

Ofgas has commissioned a poll by MORI to assess the success of competition so far. MORI questioned 1100 people in the first pilot area in October and November, and the findings will be published in around ten days.
Webb said the poll showed 86 percent of people in the pilot area are aware there have been changes in the gas supply market.

Competition was considered a "good idea" by 66 percent of respondents, with 11 percent saying it was a "bad idea". Changing supplier was rated "easy" by 79 percent of respondents, with only 12 percent finding the process "not easy". And 72 percent of those who have switched claimed they were satisfied with their decision, against only four percent who were dissatisfied, according to the poll.
Webb was asked if the move away from a single supplier to a system of multiple suppliers would compromise security of supply.

He acknowledged that over 4,000 supply points in Prestonlinks, east of Glasgow, were switched off last winter as pressure in the system dropped to dangerously low levels, and it took five days to restore pressure and reconnect all householders.

As well as the inconvenience to customers, this problem tied up significant numbers from TransCo's engineering divison for all that time, checking that all domestic appliances were switched off before reconnection and checking again that all pilot lights were lit after supply was restored.
But he added that this was mainly caused by interruptible customers failing to turn off their supplies when instructed.
"Security of supply shouldn't be an issue, as people shouldn't use any more gas just because they've changed suppliers", he said.
